data.title: Binance recovers its stolen $6.3B – But U.S. authorities have frozen $2.7B already
data.description:
After the largest hack in the history of crypto, Binance has announced that it has fully recovered all $6.3 billion in digital assets stolen during the cyberattack.

For those unaware, Binance initially recovered most of the stolen assets within days using company profits and emergency reserves, while the remaining 10% required additional time.

Binance makes a comeback

Well, the hack was so widespread that the operation involved more than 20,000 wallets and at least 65,000 transactions within a week, according to blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.

Of that, around $430,000 was also reportedly laundered through memecoins. Chainalysis also identified Chinese money-laundering networks as part of the cash conversion process.

But now Binance has made a complete comeback, and remarking on this 100% recovery, the exchange took to X and noted,

Once the zero-knowledge proof is generated, users can independently verify that their assets are backed at a minimum of 1:1.

It further added,

To our users and community: thank you for your patience and understanding.

This coincided with Binance publishing an updated Proof of Reserves snapshot dated 12th November. According to reports, user BTC holdings rose 0.35% to 687,900 BTC, while ETH reserves increased 1.04% to 3.48 million ETH.

Meanwhile, BNB holdings also climbed 1.03% to 42.95 million tokens. However, USDT reserves declined 3.68% to 24.3 billion tokens.

Fund sezuire scales up

However, the U.S. federal authorities and private-sector partners have frozen more than $2.7 billion in cryptocurrency stolen during the Binance cyberattack.

At the same time, the U.S. Department of Justice also secured court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in stolen assets as efforts to trace the remaining funds continue.

This further coincided with the U.S. Department of Justice’s announcement of coordinated actions against North Korean cybercriminal operations responsible for cryptocurrency thefts worth billions of dollars.

In fact, one major operation, called FaceStealer, has reportedly stolen more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the past 18 months.

Additionally, the FBI also seized cloud infrastructure used in the campaign and more than 900 webcam videos of victims.

Final Summary

  • The operation involved more than 20,000 wallets and at least 65,000 transactions within a week.
  • U.S. federal authorities froze more than $2.7 billion, whereas the U.S. DOJ restrained more than $1.2 billion in stolen assets.

data.title: Bitcoin volatility falls to 45% – Here’s what it does NOT mean for BTC
data.description:
Crypto evaluation, especially for Bitcoin [BTC], tends to be shifting from highly volatile to a mature asset. Bitcoin volatility has fallen to 45% over its 18 years of existence, within the range of common large-cap U.S. stocks.

For instance, JPMorgan and Amazon are at 80% and 90%, respectively, meaning they are a bit more volatile than BTC. Oracle, Coinbase, Micron, and Sandisk are more stable, with their volatilities well below 20%.

This current reading of Bitcoin volatility reflects an asset that has matured with greater institutional participation. However, this does not mean that BTC is now a low-risk asset.

Therefore, the asset deserves another risk framework different from how it was viewed in the past 10 years. During its initial stages, the volatility was exceeding 100% against a capitalization of single-digit billions.

Interestingly, during periods of strong positive momentum, Bitcoin’s gains were achieved faster than the downside deviation as per the Sortino ratio. Still, that does not negate sudden and more aggressive nosedives.

Therefore, maturity has been driven by clearer regulations, more secure investment vehicles like ETFs, and institutional involvement. BlackRock, Grayscale, Strategy, and Morgan Stanley are a few of the deeply involved institutions in BTC adoption.

Crypto sectors less dependent on Bitcoin’s performance

The maturity of Bitcoin has created opportunities for a more diversified crypto portfolio. Other crypto sectors are becoming less tied to Bitcoin’s price performance, an edge ahead of traditional assets.

Most traditional assets are related to one another.

For instance, the annualized volatility of Smart Contracts Platforms is at 58%, with BTC contributing 38% while sector-specific drive was 20%.

However, Artificial Intelligence (AI) was at 85%, probably because it was somehow new in the financial markets. For this, Bitcoin-driven volatility was 35%, while sector-specific was 50%.

Events like the resignation of the CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, after having an affair with a Chinese spy, have greatly impacted the AI market sector.

Other sectors in crypto, like financials, are at 59%, with 30% being Bitcoin-driven. This phenomenon is quite evident with seasonality in the crypto market.

But Bitcoin seasons are characterized by selective altcoin performance. On the other hand, altcoin seasons have BTC being performed by more than 75 alts in the top 100 by capitalization. Currently, only 45 altcoins have performed better than Bitcoin in the past 90 days.

All in all, crypto maturity is not only on Bitcoin but also in the whole sector. Therefore, a crypto risk framework should be done across more than one dimension to reflect its evolution.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin volatility has fallen to around 45%, reflecting a greater market maturity and institutional participation. 
  • Crypto sectors are becoming less dependent on Bitcoin’s performance, contrary to how most large-cap U.S. stocks are related.

data.title: Can TRX/ETH extend its 23% rally after Tron takes the lead with USDT?
data.description:
A key shift is taking shape in the market, and it is one traders should keep a close eye on. 

On a macro level, the stablecoin market is currently at one of its lowest levels since the 2022 bear market. The total supply of Tether (USDT) has fallen by almost $15 billion from its peak of $310 billion in mid-May. This indicated that liquidity has been flowing out of the crypto market, which is why demand has been pretty low even though Bitcoin is now trading almost 30% off its $126K high.

As the largest stablecoin hub, Ethereum has taken a significant hit too.

According to DeFiLlama, the total amount of stablecoins on Ethereum fell by over $20 billion. This was compounded by Tether as in the last 30 days alone, the total supply of USDT on Ethereum fell by nearly 9% to just over $66 billion. The key takeaway, however, may be Tron’s USDT supply. 

As shown in the chart above, USDT supply on the Tron blockchain was down by only just over 1% at press time. This was much lower than the 9% decrease seen on Ethereum. This hinted at a clear divergence in stablecoin liquidity between the two networks.

With Ethereum seeing heavier USDT outflows, Tron’s share of total USDT supply climbed above 52%, reinforcing its position as the dominant network for USDT liquidity. 

Interestingly, Tron founder Justin Sun also pointed out this trend in a recent X post, highlighting data from Token Terminal. In the past 12 months, TRON recorded a $16.1 billion hike in stablecoin supply, the highest among 45 tracked blockchains. HyperEVM came second. Arc also had an increase of $1.3 billion while Arbitrum decreased by $4.3 billion. On the contrary, Ethereum saw a more significant $30.6 billion decline. 

In short, Tron’s [TRX] stablecoin dominance may be taking down Ethereum. It is also making inroads into other major Layer 1 networks. According to AMBCrypto, with increasing liquidity advantages, TRX is an altcoin to watch when the market moves back into a risk-on environment.

Tron’s stablecoin inflows challenge Ethereum as TRX/ETH gains 23%

The real impact of this divergence becomes clearer when looking at on-chain activity. 

Interestingly, data from the Tron network also seemed to confirm the stablecoins trend. Within a 24-hour period, Tron processed 12,990,075 transactions. This is the highest daily total for the past 7 days, averaging at around 150 transactions per second (TPS). This suggested that there may be consistent demand on the network, with the increase in stablecoins on Tron being due to real demand.

The result? The TRX/ETH ratio has risen by over 23% so far in Q4 and was only 15% away from making up all of its Q3 losses. On top of that, with stablecoin liquidity and on-chain activity between the two projects increasing, this trend may be accelerating.

If this continues, a break above the 0.002-resistance level could become more likely, opening the door for further TRX outperformance against ETH. 

Taken together, with increasing stablecoin dominance, high volume, and the 23% rally in the TRX/ETH ratio, 0.002 is a key level. If it breaks through it could be a testement to TRX’s strength, while a failure to clear resistance may leave the pair trading within its current range. 

As it stands, the combination of stablecoin inflows and growing network activity means that TRON is well-positioned to outperform Ethereum [ETH] this quarter.

Final Summary

data.title: Ethereum’s store-of-value narrative is gaining traction – From Joseph Lubin, at least
data.description:
Ethereum’s “store-of-value” narrative is gaining traction lately.

Looking at the broader picture, there are several factors that are leading to increased risk sentiment in the U.S. market.

Whether it be fears over an AI bubble, high-interest rates, CPI figures, or the aftermath of the mid-term elections, Bitcoin is heading toward its worst annual cycle since the 2022 bear market, with year-to-date losses approaching 17% in 2026.

Keeping this in mind, while Ethereum has suffered nearly twice Bitcoin’s losses and is looking at its worst year since 2022, co-founder Joseph Lubin is bullish over the future potential of Ethereum as an inflationary hedge.

Highlighting several key trends on-chain, he says that Ethereum has long-term potential to outperform both Bitcoin and gold as a store of value.

One of the main reasons for his argument is because of the DeFi ecosystem, stablecoins, and smart contracts on Ethereum. These allow ETH to have a stronger utility base compared to Bitcoin and gold.

In addition, with AI adoption accelerating, Ethereum could also see rising demand for its network infrastructure.

Ethereum’s macro hedge thesis faces a crucial market test

Ethereum’s inflation-hedge narrative faces a key test.

As previously mentioned, the U.S. market is facing a range of risks. This has made this one of the most volatile times for investors. So far, Ethereum has had trouble attracting risk capital, falling almost 30% during Q4 compared to Bitcoin, which has fallen only 17%.

This puts Joseph Lubin’s thesis under pressure, as Bitcoin continues to lead the store-of-value narrative while Ethereum struggles to keep up.

Gold, meanwhile, is also losing steam. The metal is trading in a technical downtrend with losses of more than 5% so far in Q4, as it has failed to move above $4,000. The most recent fall below this level has caused a loss of around $480 billion in market value in just 10 hours.

That said, gold still has a clear “relative-strength” advantage over crypto.

As the chart above shows, the ETH/XAU ratio has lost more than 19% in Q4, demonstrating that Ethereum has failed to make any progress relative to gold. This becomes a key level to monitor. A breakout could result in better technical support for Lubin’s long-term thesis.

For now, Ethereum is struggling to outperform Bitcoin and gold currently. Despite rising staking participation and stronger network security, ETH is yet to translate these fundamentals into stronger capital inflows or relative price performance.

Final Summary

data.title: Why Strategy’s MSCI removal could spell trouble for Bitcoin’s Q4 outlook
data.description:
If you thought Q4 volatility was finally cooling down, you might want to think again.

And yes, the December rate decision priced in by the market is only the tip of the iceberg. Analysts have spent much of the last 24 hours assessing the MSCI report announcing its index review on the 11th of November. Naturally, the focus immediately shifted to Strategy’s MSTR index eligibility as traders began pricing in the risk of its removal from MSIC’s global indexes. Notably, this is exactly how things played out.

In its recent review, MSCI has officially confirmed that Strategy will be removed from its global indexes, effective from the 1st of December. This put MSTR among the companies set to lose their place in these benchmarks, adding another layer of uncertainty around institutional exposure and potential selling pressure.

However, to understand why this decision matters, it is important to first understand what MSCI represents.

MSCI (Morgan Stanley Capital International) creates some of the biggest stock indices in the world. Investment funds that have over $21 trillion in assets track these indices. Many invest in stocks according to these indices. If the fund tracks an MSCI index including MSTR, then the Strategy removal may cause these investment funds to decrease or sell their holdings to match the new index. 

It, therefore, comes as little surprise that traders are worried that MSTR’s removal by MSCI will cause a wave of institutional selling. Moreover, given that Strategy is still the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin [BTC] (850,364 BTC on their balance sheet), the importance of this decision cannot be understated. Less institutional exposure to MSTR could cause sentiment to turn more negative towards corporate Bitcoin treasuries. 

Traders are now watching whether the removal triggers a broader risk-off move across the crypto market.

MSTR institutional holdings rise 9.62% as MSCI removal looms

Following MSCI’s decision, MSTR’s institutional ownership is becoming an important part of the story. 

Some of Wall Street’s largest asset management firms also hold large stakes within the company, such as Capital International Investors, BlackRock, Morgan Stanley, Invesco, and Goldman Sachs. Based on the latest institutional filings, it can be seen that Capital International Investors is the largest institutional investor holding around 34.9 million MSTR shares. This is followed by BlackRock with 19.39 million shares.

Interestingly, institutional investment increased within Q2. Invesco increased their shareholding by around 7.21 million shares. Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs increased theirs by 4.02 million shares, Capital International Investors increased theirs by 3.46 million shares and BlackRock increased their shareholding by around 1.64 million shares. Overall, there were around 209.52 million MSTR shares owned by institutional investors at the end of Q2, an increase of 9.62% compared to the previous quarter. 

However, not every major institution was accumulating. 

The move by Capital Research Global Investors, who shed around 4.62 million shares, and Bank of America, who sold 2.79 million, demonstrates that it was already a slightly negative time for institutions. The primary concern therefore will be whether MSCI’s decision to exclude MSTR may speed up institutional selling.

In this context, MSCI’s latest decision could become a turning point for Bitcoin’s late Q4 rally. If the funds tracking MSCI’s indices are forced to sell their MSTR stake, it will add more downward pressure. It may also damage institutional confidence in Strategy’s “high-risk, Bitcoin-focused” investment strategy. In turn, creating further uncertainty in the crypto markets.

Final Summary

data.title: Bitcoin dips below $70K – Will $455M in liquidations derail BTC’s price recovery?
data.description:
The crypto markets are bleeding, and so is Bitcoin [BTC], the largest of them all. The total cap of the crypto market is down over 5% in the past 24 hours, as market status turned to extreme fear.

More than $856.01 million in crypto liquidations happened with longs, equating to $771.7 million. Of the total liquidations, Bitcoin accounted for $454.7 million, with longs taking 96%.

As a result, BTC slid below $70,000 and was trading around $68,888, at press time, having lost 6% of its cap. A daily trading volume of $31.90 billion reinforced the sharp decline in price below $70,000.

For Ethereum [ETH], 91% of longs were liquidated from its total of $131.95 million. Other crypto assets saw over $218 million wiped out, with long positions representing 75%.

Can renewed spot demand support recovery?

At the same time, a Bitcoin rebound toward $71,000 was becoming more fragile considering other factors. For instance, the market sentiment from some analysts, like Benjamin Cowen, was shifting.

When replying to his post that bear market makes fools of both bulls and bears, Benjamin Bowen reiterated he thought Q4 could be weak.

This has been the case since the midterm US election results, implying investors were less optimistic as pro-crypto Republicans lost control of the house.

Additionally, monthly spot and futures demand was contracting at an accelerating rate. That of spot was at -280K BTC, while that of perpetual futures was at -82K, a total demand of -362K BTC.

Moreover, Bitcoin ETF outflows reached $300 million on the 11th of November and $48 million the following day. This indicated institutions were consistently withdrawing capital from Bitcoin and the crypto market in general. This adds institutional selling pressure to BTC.

More downside risks emanate from a spike in miner-to-exchange flows this week. The total surged to 2,077 BTC, about 16 times its 30-day average of 127 BTC.

However, it does not confirm selling, as it could mean treasury transfers or management. Though, it could mean miners’ margins are getting squeezed by low prices.

There was more to this nose dive. US demand for BTC was quiet, with the Coinbase Premium Index below -4 from 0.8 in September. This was the deepest average since February, affirming the low demand.

However, there was still a catch. The rallies of 2024 and 2025 all ran with a premium, with several of them starting from such deep discounts.

This could be driven by renewed spot demand as its CVD is closer to neutral, though the improvement did not last there. The Futures taker CVD was dominated by sellers.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin price plunged below $70,000 as liquidations surpassed $455 million, with longs accounting for 96%. 
  • Bitcoin recovery remains fragile amidst weak demand, ETF outflows, and shifting market sentiment.

data.title: Trezor slashes reseller network by 80% following hardware implant discovery – Details
data.description:
Trezor confirmed on the 12th of November that three Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by CryptoBilis contained malicious implants. Fortunately, no customer had reported losing funds.

Still, Trezor urged affected buyers to move their crypto after releasing a firmware fix.

Customers bought those 3 devices between the 20th of August and the 23rd of September through CryptoBilis directly or its Tokopedia and Shopee stores. Trezor examined one device in its lab and identified two more from customer photos.

48 buyers had contacted the company, and at press time, checks were ongoing. Trezor reported that there were no confirmed cases involving other models or resellers.

Why did Trezor urge buyers to move funds?

Apparently, the implants could take recovery phrases and passphrases that appeared on the wallet screen.

On X, a user asked how a software update could stop a physical implant from recording the display. Trezor explained that firmware could “listen to the communication between the MCU and the display,” and the firm has now changed the order of commands needed for the trigger.

Regardless, Trezor still urged buyers to use a fresh recovery phrase because “the update can’t protect a wallet backup that was captured before it.” This advice applied to customers who bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onward.

The hardware wallet company also urged those using its devices to move funds to a new wallet with a fresh recovery phrase. It told buyers with unused devices to leave them unconfigured. Eligible buyers could contact Trezor Support for a replacement or a refund where shipping limited their options.

How did the Ledger case shape Trezor’s response?

Trezor dropped CryptoBilis on the 9th of October after reports of tampered Ledger devices sold through them. A customer also flagged a suspected Safe 5 implant on the 28th of October.

Trezor issued a warning two days later, saying that it cut its reseller network by about 80% and tightened rules on sourcing, storage, and access.

This brought the debate back to what self-custody protects, and as Ledger CEO Pascal Gauthier said,

Everybody will be hacked at some point. Perfect security doesn’t exist.

 

Final Summary

  • Trezor confirmed that there were three tampered Safe 5 wallets sold through CryptoBilism, but no one had experienced losses yet.
  • However, affected buyers still need a wallet with a fresh recovery phrase.

data.title: Bitcoin dominance hits 61%, but THIS will decide when is altcoin season!
data.description:
Altcoins have been waiting for their moment all year. Bitcoin [BTC] keeps taking it from them. However, it would seem now that the latter’s market share could decide who wins the next few weeks.

The ‘undeafeated’ Bitcoin

Coinglass’s Altcoin Season Index had a reading of 42 at press time.

Anything above 75 ordinarily counts as altcoin season. This means that the press time reading still leaned towards Bitcoin.

There’s numbers to back this up too. According to CryptoRank, for instance, Bitcoin was up 16.6% over the last 90 days.

Only 31 coins on its list did better!

Bitway [BTW] has risen by about 220%, Quant [QNT] went up 184%, Midnight Network [NIGHT] by 172% and Raydium [RAY] by 152%. Stacks and NEAR also doubled on the price charts.

That’s where the excitement ends though.

A lot of the big names didn’t even keep up with BTC. Solana [SOL], for instance, went up a measly 10% over the same stretch. Binance Coin [BNB] also rose by 10.6%, and Chainlink [LINK] outdid them… with 12%.

So yes, a few altcoins are having a great run. Most of the rest are just watching Bitcoin ride off into the sunset.

Who’s the winner?

At the time of writing, BTC.D was at 60.9%.

On the weekly chart, that’s a range that’s been narrowing for more than a year. The top of that has been sliding since late 2025. The bottom has been going up from around 57%.

Right now, it’s pushing right against the top.

If dominance breaks above 61.5%, Bitcoin will maintain its lead and altcoins will stay stuck in the mud. If it diverges near 61%, that would mean that the latter group will get a little breathing room.

A drop below 58% is where things could really swing towards Ethereum [ETH] and the rest of the market though.

For context, its dominance peaked at about 66% back in mid-2025. We are nowhere near that yet.

Until then, the market should lie in wait. Altcoin holders will really want that rejection at the 61%-level though.

Final Summary

  • Only 31 altcoins surpassed Bitcoin’s 16.6% gains over the last 90 days.

  • BTC.D at 61% will decide whether altcoins can recover.

data.title: Here’s why Zcash could remove 50,000 ZEC from its grants treasury
data.description:
The Zcash [ZEC] community is gearing up to vote on a proposal that could significantly change how ZEC funds its development and distributes newly created tokens. The plan involves removing 50,000 ZEC from the Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) treasury and redirecting its value toward future mining rewards.

That said, Zcash currently allocates 8% of newly issued ZEC to ZCG, which uses the funds to support developers, wallet providers, and other ecosystem projects.

These grants help maintain the infrastructure and software needed to use ZEC. However, rising ZEC prices has increased the value of ZCG’s existing treasury, which has raised concerns that the committee was accumulating more funds than necessary while continuing to receive new token allocations.

All about Zcash’s new proposal

However, now, under the new proposal, approximately 55% of ZCG’s treasury (50,000 ZEC) would be removed from circulation within 30 days of activation. Going ahead, its value would be credited to the Network Sustainability Mechanism, introduced through the NU7 upgrade. This, in turn, would gradually return ZEC to the network through future mining rewards.

At the same time, the proposal would also end ZCG’s existing 8% allocation of newly created ZEC. Instead, this share would accumulate in a new Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund until the next halving takes place.

As this happens, the fund would remain inaccessible until a separate proposal establishes withdrawal rules. Lastly, ZCG would retain its remaining treasury to continue funding development, while the separate 12% Coinholder-Controlled Fund would remain unchanged.

How is Zcash’s new proposal different from the old one?

For those unaware, the revised plan follows ZCG’s 3rd November decision to abandon an earlier proposal, which faced criticism for seeking to redirect approximately 98,000 ZEC from existing assets and future income toward mining rewards.

So, now, the next step is community voting, which is scheduled from 16th November to 30th November. Coinholders and community panels will assess the proposal’s support.

If it receives rough consensus, developers, and miners can work toward implementing it through a future network upgrade called NU7.1. However, there is no confirmed activation date yet. 

Zcash market dynamics paint a mixed picture

This coincided with Zcash’s monthly active developer count having nearly doubled over the past two years.

According to Glassnode’s report, around 70% of its active developers have more than one year of experience in crypto development, compared with 58% across the wider industry.

Still, ZEC’s price action was under bearish pressure as it was trading at $986.40 at press time after a drop of 1.4% in the past 24 hours.

This followed a recent report by AMBCrypto wherein ZEC fell by 15.25% and Open Interest also declined 13.4%, indicating weakening speculative demand.

Final Summary

  • Approximately 55% of ZCG’s treasury would be removed from circulation within 30 days of activation.
  • The revised plan came after ZCG’s 3rd November decision was rejected due to the expected 98,000 ZEC figure.

data.title: USDT fell below $1 – That’s how thin crypto liquidity has gotten
data.description:
The crypto market is at a critical point with its stablecoin liquidity continuing to shrink as the year nears its end. Over the past four weeks, more than $14.20 billion in stablecoins have left the market.

Currently, the stablecoin market cap has declined below $300 billion, which is its lowest level in 14 months. That is, the cap plunged from $313 billion to $298 billion, the fastest contraction since June 2022.

Additionally, Tether’s USDT was trading below $1 at the time of press, showing that the stablecoin’s buying power was weakening too.

This contraction implies that crypto liquidity in the market is thin and fresh capital is limited to support a bullish recovery. Both Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] have been averagely on a decline when gauging this month’s performance.

This suggests that both BTC and the broader altcoin market are bearish. Thus, the stablecoin supply did not necessarily go into buying and holding like in the previous years.

Bitcoin derivatives and spot demand shrink

Meanwhile, Bitcoin’s price remained heavily influenced by liquidation-driven moves rather than organic spot demand. As per the Binance Liquidation Accumulation Index, the volatility was driven by two-way liquidations.

Between September and November, the index has visited the upper and lower bands, at 80 and 20, respectively, more than three times each. This implies that both longs and shorts are being wiped out at this juncture.

With that, the price of BTC could continue bouncing between $60K and $87K until either bears or bulls win the battle.

At the same time, Spot demand was struggling to provide consistent support.

For instance, Binance Buy/Sell Delta has declined from 0.07 to below the neutral level, affirming the weak spot demand. In fact, traders on the exchange were selling.

Additionally, U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of over $1.60 billion over the past 20 sessions. Over the past 24 hours, around $299.90 million exited the BTC ETFs market.

Similarly, Ethereum and Solana ETFs lost $144.81 million and $5.85 million, respectively, while those of Binance Coin [BNB] and XRP remained inactive.

Therefore, if crypto liquidity and spot demand do not return, then a general market recovery would be hard to materialize. Thus, a turnback to stablecoin market cap growth would be the first sign of new money.

Final Summary

  • Crypto liquidity contracted by over $14.20 billion as the stablecoin market fell below $300 billion for the first time in 14 months. 
  • Bitcoin was seeing weak spot demand and two-way liquidations, reinforcing its price stagnation between $67K and $87K levels.
